News global nation business lifestyle entertainment technology sports opinion LATEST NEWS STORIES HEADLINES METRO REGIONS NATION WORLD CDN NEWSLETTER www / Comelec dismisses ‘no-el’ in 2028 claims anew By: Dianne Sampang - @inquirerdotnet INQUIRER.net / 02:49 PM November 22, 2026 Share: MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has once again dismissed resurfacing claims that there will be a “no-el” (no elections) scenario in 2028 as it emphasized that the poll body is currently preparing for the much-anticipated elections.
In an interview with dzBB on Sunday, Comelec chair George Erwin Garcia was asked about recent claims that there will be no elections in 2028.
“Imposibleng mangyari. Ang Saligang Batas ang nagsasabing may eleksyon sa 2028. Walang kahit na anong batas ang pwedeng gawin ng kongreso, pirmahan ng pangulo ang makakapagbago sa Saligang Batas. Therefore, 100 percent naming ginagarantiya sa sambayanan na may halalan po tayo sa 2028.,” Garcia answered.
(That is impossible to happen. The 1987 Constitution says that there shall be elections in 2028. The Congress cannot make any law that will be signed by the president to change the Constitution. Therefore, we guarantee 100 percent that there will be elections in 2028.)
READ: Hernandez debunks claim House is hatching ‘no-el’ plan
The Article VII, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution mandates that the president and vice president of the country must be elected for a term of six years, with their terms beginning at noon on the 30th day of June of the same election year.
This came after Atty. Paolo Panelo, spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte, said in an interview with Bilyonaryo News Channel that he had a conversation with Duterte where she said that she received information for a “no-el” plan in 2028.
Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez on Thursday debunked the claims that members of House of Representatives are forming plans to postpone the 2028 elections.
Garcia then said that the elections for the president and vice president cannot be likened to Barangay and Sangguniang Elections where they can be postponed or have their terms shortened or extended.
READ: Comelec: ‘No election’ via Constitutional amendment not possible
“Sa president and vice president, di pwedeng baguhin ang termino sapagkat wala tayong hold over capacity. Matatapos at matatapos ang kanilang termino, June 30 tanghali ng 2028,” he added.
(The terms of the president and vice president cannot be changed because we don’t have a hold over capacity. Their terms will end at noon of June 30, 2028.)
Garcia also shared updates on Comelec’s preparations for the 2028 elections, noting that the filing of certificates of candidacy (COC) will be scheduled on September 20-26, 2027.
Garcia earlier said that the poll body will open the period filing of COCs earlier than the usual timeline of the first week of October so they can resolve disputes on candidacies and can immediately start printing of official ballots.
Aside from this, he said that the poll body began the bidding process for the internet voting system and transmission services. He added that the procurement process for the automated counting machines (ACMs) will start by December this year.

Garcia also said that the poll body will allocate P22 billion for the leasing of the ACMs, which is the same mechanism it used for the 2025 midterm elections. However, he clarified that the ACMs used in the previous elections will not be used in the 2028 elections as the machines have to be brand new. /ms
